In summary, our research is concerned with
the thermalization process of an expanding parton system in high-energy nuclear reactions.
the study of the early stage evolution of the parton system in relativistic nuclear collisions.
the study of the thermalization process in a high-energy nuclear collision.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the thermalization process of partons is a very complicated one.
the parton system does thermalize, and that the thermalization process can be understood in terms of a time-dependent relaxation-time approximation.
we are not able to predict the entropy produced in a nuclear collision, but we have shown that the entropy production depends strongly on the initial conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the entropy production due collisions is not negligible and the final state entropy depends on the initial condition and on the time of the collisions.
the parton-gas system does not thermalize in the sense of reaching equilibrium in the early stages of the collision.
the parton system thermalizes only gradually, and the final state is sensitive to the early parton production, which is still not well understood.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the parton system does thermalize but only after a phase of free expansion where a considerable amount of entropy is produced (due to the collision terms).
entropy is not a conserved quantity, but is a function of the system.
the entropy produced during the prethermalization phase of an expanding system is a crucial part of the entropy budget in a heavy-ion collision.
